name: eth.zig (secp256k1 signing)
baseline: k256 (RustCrypto secp256k1 crate, as used by alloy.rs/alloy-signer)
workload: secp256k1 ECDSA sign and sign+recover, custom criterion-style harness with 0.5s warmup and 2s measurement window, on Apple Silicon
claimed_speedup: secp256k1_sign: 2.34x faster (22,033 ns vs 51,490 ns); secp256k1_sign_recover: 4.23x faster (52,095 ns vs 220,150 ns) vs alloy.rs (k256 0.13 backend)
hardware: Apple Silicon (aarch64-macos); exact chip model (M1/M2/M3/M4) not specified
tradeoffs: eth.zig's own README states its secp256k1 speed win comes from vendoring bitcoin-core/secp256k1 (already-catalogued C library) as the backend, not novel Zig crypto; the library also loses 5/26 and ties 3/26 of the other benchmarked operations (e.g. hex parsing, UniswapV4 swap math) against alloy.rs.
caveats: First-party benchmark run by the project itself; hardware stated only as 'Apple Silicon' rather than an exact CPU model, so it falls short of tier A. The repo's own historical note shows the score has drifted over time (23/26 in March 2026 vs 18/26 in June 2026 after alloy.rs optimized several paths), indicating the margin is not stable.
found_via: Hacker News: search queries "faster ECDSA" and "zig crypto fast" surfaced "Show HN: Eth.zig - Pure Zig Ethereum library, 19/26 benchmark wins vs. alloy.rs" (2026-02-27)

name: watsign
workload: Ed25519 sign and verify of short and long messages, warm (50x average after 50x warmup) and cold-start timings, in-browser via puppeteer
claimed_speedup: 4-6x faster than tweetnacl-js warmed up, up to 33x faster on cold start after page load; 1.2-3x faster than noble-ed25519 warmed up, up to 17x on cold start
tradeoffs: JS/WebAssembly only, not usable directly from C++; ports the TweetNaCl algorithm rather than a novel design; API is async-only because of WebAssembly plus native SHA-512; signing/verification only, no encryption support.
caveats: First-party benchmark on the project's own repo (comparison scripts present: src-experiments/test/perf.js, performance.js, test-tweetnacl-js.js, test-noble-ed25519.js, test-watsign.js); numbers are from 2021 on Chromium 93 and have not been revalidated on modern engines/hardware; the 'up to 33x' figure is a cold-start outlier versus the more representative 4-6x warm-run figure; last commit 2024-04-15, over two years stale as of today.
found_via: Hacker News: search query "faster Ed25519" surfaced "Tweetnacl's ed25519 signatures, ported to WebAssembly, 5x faster" (2021-12-22)
